saints.name: St. Charles Lwanga and Companions
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: The young royal pages of Buganda who chose death by fire rather than betray their baptism…
biography: Charles Lwanga was born about 1860 in the kingdom of Buganda, in present-day Uganda, and rose to be chief of the royal pages at the court of King Mwanga II. In 1885 the king had the Anglican bishop James Hannington killed, then beheaded Joseph Mukasa, the Catholic catechist who reproached him; Charles and about a hundred catechumens sought baptism from the White Fathers, Charles himself on 15 November.

In May 1886 Mwanga, enraged that his pages would neither renounce their faith nor yield to his immoral demands, condemned the Christians to death. Charles secretly baptized the boys still unbaptized, among them the youngest, Kizito; on the march to the execution ground at Namugongo, three of the company were killed.

On 3 June 1886 Charles was burned alive apart from the rest, and twelve more Catholics, together with nine Anglicans, perished in the flames, while others died by the club or in the later persecution. Twenty-two Catholic martyrs of Uganda were canonized by Pope Paul VI on 18 October 1964, the first canonized martyrs of modern Africa, honoured as patrons of converts and of African youth.
saints.knownFor: The first canonized martyrs of sub-Saharan Africa.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Charles Lwanga and Companions (vatican.va)
